questions.question: The marked price of an article was Rs.400 but the shopkeeper offered a double discount of 25% and 15%. How much did he finally sell the article for?
questions.solution:
Given: 

The marked price of an article was Rs.400.

The shopkeeper offered a double discount of 25% and 15%.

Concept used:

Final discount percentage after two successive discounts of A% and B% = (A + B - {AB over 100})\%

Selling price = Marked Price - Marked Price × Discount%

Calculation:

Final resultant discount = 25 + 15 - (25 × 15)/100 = 36.25%

Now, the final selling price = 400 - 400 × 36.25%

⇒ 400 - 145 = Rs. 255

∴ He finally sold the article for Rs. 255.

questions.question: The difference of between two positive number x and y (x > y) is 350. If 9.5% of x is equal to 16.5% of y then the sum of the two numbers x and y is :
questions.solution:
Given:

The difference between two positive numbers x and y (x > y) is 350.

9.5% of x is equal to 16.5% of y.

Calculation:

According to the question,

x - y = 350 ....(1)

9.5% of x = 16.5% of y

⇒ 0.095x = 0.165y

⇒ x/y = 0.165/0.095

⇒ (x + y)/(x - y) = (0.165 + 0.095)/(0.165 - 0.095) (Using componendo-dividendo method)

⇒ (x + y)/350 = 0.26/0.07 (From 1)

⇒ (x + y)/50 = 26

⇒ (x + y) = 26 × 50

⇒ (x + y) = 1300

**∴ The value of (x + y) is 1300.**

questions.question: 40 kg of an alloy A is mixed with 63 kg of alloy B. If alloy A has lead and tin in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 and alloy B has tin and copper in the ratio 2 ∶ 5, then find the amount of tin in the new alloy ?
questions.solution:
Given:

40 kg of an alloy A is mixed with 63 kg of alloy B. 

Alloy A has lead and tin in the ratio 2 ∶ 3.

Alloy B has tin and copper in the ratio 2 ∶ 5.

Calculation:

Amount of tin in 40 kg alloy A = 40 × 3/(2 + 3) = 24 kg

Amount of tin in 63 kg alloy B = 63 × 2/(2 + 5) = 18 kg

Total amount of tin the new alloy = 24 + 18 = 42 kg

∴ The amount of tin in the new alloy is 42 kg.

questions.question: Find the Simple interest on Rs. 2,400 from 20 March 2019 to 31 may 2019 at 6{1 over 4}% rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 2400

Rate of interest = 6{1 over 4}% = 6.25%

Concept used:

1 year = 365 days

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Days between 20 March 2019 to 31 may 2019 = 73 days

Now, the simple interest incurred on Rs. 2400 for 73 days

⇒ (2400 × 6.25 × 73/365)/100

⇒ (2400 × 6.25 × 0.2)/100

⇒ Rs. 30

**∴ Simple interest incurred on Rs. 2,400 from 20 March 2019 to 31 May 2019 at 6{1 over 4}% rate is Rs. 30.**

questions.question: A car runs the first 272 km at an average speed of 40 km/h and the next 85 km at an average speed of 50 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = 272 + 85 = 357 km

Total Time = (272 ÷ 40) + (85 ÷ 50) = 6.8 + 1.7 = 8.5 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 357 ÷ 8.5 = 42 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of 1st part (D₁) = 272 km, Speed (S₁) = 40 km/h

Distance of 2ⁿd part (D₂) = 85 km, Speed (S₂) = 50 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51dc88701835611c9c586e0afb8a34dec16b05d33d6c145d6f6e29d7fc3f9713.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 272 + 85 = 357 km

⇒ Time for 1st part (T₁) = 272 ÷ 40 = 6.8 hours

⇒ Time for 2ⁿd part (T₂) = 85 ÷ 50 = 1.7 hours

⇒ Total Time = T₁ + T₂ = 6.8 + 1.7 = 8.5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 357 ÷ 8.5

⇒ Average Speed = 3570 ÷ 85 = 42 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a person covers equal distances at speeds x and y, then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a person travels for equal time intervals at speeds x and y, then Average Speed = (x + y) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction at speeds x and y (where x > y), Relative Speed = x − y. For objects moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = x + y.

questions.question: If the selling price is tripled, the profit becomes four times. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Given:

If the selling price is tripled, the profit becomes four times. 

Concept used:

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Cost Price = Selling Price - Profit

Calculation:

Let the selling price and profit be S and M respectively.

So, the cost price = (S - M)

When the selling price is 3S, profit is 4M.

So, again the cost price = (3S - 4M)

According to the question,

S - M = 3S - 4M

⇒ 2S = 3M

⇒ S = 1.5M

The cost price becomes = S - M

⇒ 1.5M - M = 0.5M

The selling price = S = 1.5M

Now, profit% = {{1.5M - 0.5M} over 0.5M} times 100\% = 200%

∴ The profit percentage is 200%.

questions.question: The ratio of two positive numbers is 11 ∶ 17 and their HCF is 4. Their LCM is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of two positive numbers is 11 ∶ 17 and their HCF is 4.

Concept used:

HCF of two or more numbers is the greatest factor that divides the numbers.

Calculation:

Since the HCF of the two numbers is 4, the two numbers are as follows:

11 × 4 = 44 and 17 × 4 = 68

LCM (44, 68) = 4 × 11 × 17 = 748

∴ Their LCM is 748.

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers a discount of 12% on a sofa-set and sells it for Rs. 17,776 What is the marked price (in Rs.) of the sofa-set?
questions.solution:

A shopkeeper offers a discount of 12% on a sofa-set and sells it for Rs. 17,776.

Concept used:

Selling price = Marked Price - Marked Price × Discount%

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount%)

Calculation:

⇒ 0.88P = 17776

⇒ P = 17776/0.88

⇒ P = 20200

∴ The marked price of the sofa-set is Rs. 20,200.

questions.question: Mohan and Ramesh can together complete a work in 15 days. Mohan is 50% more effiecient than Ramesh. The time taken by Mohan alone to complete the work is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Mohan and Ramesh can together complete a work in 15 days. 

Mohan is 50% more efficient than Ramesh. 

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken 

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of Ramesh be R units a day.

So, efficiency of Mohan = R + 50% of R = 1.5R units

Total work = 15 × (R + 1.5R) = 37.5R units

Now, the time taken by Mohan alone to complete the work = 37.5R/1.5R = 25 days

**∴ The time taken by Mohan alone to complete the work is 25 days.**

questions.question: A can do a work in 18 days. A and B working together can do the same work in 8 days, whereas B and C working together can do the same work in 6 days. In how many days can A, B and C working together do the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A can do a work in 18 days. A and B working together can do the same work in 8 days, whereas B and C working together can do the same work in 6 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day (Efficiency) × Total time taken 

Calculation:

Let the efficiencies of A, B, and C be P, Q, and R units respectively.

According to the question,

Total work = 18 × P = 18P ....(1)

Total work = 8 × (P + Q) = 8(P + Q) ....(2)

Total work = 6 × (Q + R) = 6(Q + R) ....(3)

Equating (1) & (2),

18P = 8(P + Q)

⇒ 18P = 8P + 8Q

⇒ 10P = 8Q

⇒ 5P = 4Q

⇒ Q = 1.25P ....(4)

Equating (2) & (3),

8(P + Q) = 6(Q + R)

⇒ 8P + 8Q = 6Q + 6R

⇒ 8P + 10P = 7.5P + 6R (From 4)

⇒ 10.5P = 6R

⇒ R = 1.75P ....(5)

Efficiencies of A, B, and C = P + Q + R

⇒ P + 1.25P + 1.75P = 4P

Now, the required days by A, B, and C working together do the same work

⇒ 18P/4P = 4 {1{} over 2} days

**∴ A, B, and C working together will take 4 {1{} over 2} days to complete the work.**

⇒ 1380 × M% = 1449 - 1380
